title: A morphism which is flat away from a relative effective Cartier divisor is flat everywhere
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a morphism which is flat at every point outside a relative effective Cartier divisor is flat at every point of the source (statement lines 4141-4146). The counted proof, 21 lines, is not a restatement: it states the equivalent algebra fact about a ring map A to B and a nonzerodivisor h, produces the explicit short exact sequence relating B, its localization B_h and the colimit of the quotients (1/h^n)B/B, observes that the middle and right terms are flat, and then justifies flatness of the colimit by a second displayed exact sequence plus induction on n, using two cited algebra lemmas about flatness along short exact sequences and filtered colimits (proof lines 4148-4167). It is H2 under the lane rule that a short proof containing a checkable construction is still H2; the closing sentence of the proof leaves routine details to the reader, and those concern the translation step rather than the displayed argument.
